correctness.rationale: Exact domain: for every integer m≥1, two agents have independently sampled Uniform(0,1) cardinal additive marginal values for m indivisible goods, allocated to the larger-value agent. Both envy events are mutually exclusive since their utility differences sum to Σ|X−Y|>0, and exchangeability makes them equiprobable. The signed first-agent variable has density f(z)=1+z for -1<z<0 and f(z)=z for 0<z<1, MGF [e^t(t−1)+t+e^(−t)]/t². Expanding M(t)^m and using the explicit inverse bilateral Laplace transform proves the exact rational formula. Convexity gives a unique negative θ with M′(θ)=0; tilting at θ and the bounded nonlattice density local CLT gives the exact 2ρ^m/(|θ|σ√(2πm)) prefactor. The included checker passed six rational identities, independent two-item order statistics, six direct simulations and tilt-moment calculations; an independently discretized density convolution agreed through m=12. Numerical tests do not certify the infinite theorem; the stated proof supplies that argument.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary sources give qualitative asymptotic welfare-optimal fairness or worst-case complexity, but no exact rational probability formula for every m or sharp exponential rate/prefactor in the iid two-agent Uniform(0,1) model. Three focused searches of published research records yielded only adjacent ordinal-assignment and stochastic-invariant results. The known broader eventual-fairness theorem is acknowledged, and no novelty is claimed for the mechanism or convergence alone.
residual_risks: No search can exclude unindexed, unpublished, or independently derived exact two-agent uniform convolution formulas.

value.rationale: The exact finite-sample risk of envy under the canonical efficient greedy allocation is a natural, policy-relevant object that known high-probability existence statements do not quantify. The new rational formula determines the exact reliability for arbitrary m, and the sharp rate plus prefactor yields mathematically calibrated large-item confidence budgets. The result is an infinite-family quantitative classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; its significant mathematical content is the explicit inversion and tight local-limit asymptotic, not simply code or a generic Chernoff bound.
